## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the night journey and on the ascent that later tradition links with it. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names Jerusalem, Isra, Miraj and Buraq and the place of the farthest mosque.
- The Arabic for the first mosque (a descriptive epithet) is rendered 'inviolable'; the common rendering is 'sacred'. A scholar should decide the wording.
- Whether the journey was in body or in spirit was disputed by earlier scholars and the ayah does not settle it; this draft takes no side.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Glory to Him who took His servant  (`#glory-to-him-who-took-his-servant`)

Cited ayat: 17:1

> **17:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًا مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْأَقْصَا ٱلَّذِى بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ

### Claims

**c1** (17:1): Glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed.

**c2** (17:1): The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs.

**c3** (17:1): He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

### One-minute summary

The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. It says the purpose was to show him some of Our signs [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs [c2]. He is the Hearing, the Seeing [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah has one sentence of praise, one of purpose and one that names God as the Hearing and the Seeing, all around a journey told in a single clause [c1][c2][c3]. It names no person, no vehicle, no duration and no time of the night [c1].

### Kids mode

God took His servant by night from one mosque to a farthest mosque [c1]. It was to show him some of God's signs [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah begins with glory to God before it states the journey, as the wording of the ayah shows [c1]. Another is that the journey's purpose is stated as showing signs [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the servant is; the ayah does not name him.
- Not established: how the journey was made, how long it took, whether it was bodily or in vision, or what the signs were that he was shown.
- Not established: what the farthest mosque was or where, beyond the ayah's words about blessed surroundings.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the servant, the starting place and the farthest mosque by name, the vehicle, the ascent, the meetings with earlier prophets and the date.
